title: Supreme Court rejects Tamil Nadu's plea for extra Cauvery water; lets Karnataka bike taxis run
dek: Tamil Nadu had sought 11 TMC that it said Karnataka owed; in a separate case the court upheld a High Court ruling allowing Ola, Uber and Rapido bike taxis.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed two applications by Tamil Nadu seeking a direction to Karnataka to release an extra 11 TMC (thousand million cubic feet) of Cauvery water, and in a separate case cleared the way for bike taxis to keep running across Karnataka, according to reports of the day's hearings.

## Cauvery

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh rejected Tamil Nadu's request for the shortfall it said had built up by 7 October to be made up at Biligundlu, the measuring station on the inter-state border, at a rate of 1.3 TMC a day for ten days. "The application is dismissed," the bench said, according to reports; it also said it would dismiss a third application to place more documents on record. The court's reasons were not reported.

Tamil Nadu argued that it was asking only for its proportionate share in a distress year, that Karnataka should not pass the full burden of a weak monsoon downstream while using its own reservoirs for irrigation, and that its farmers' crops had already suffered, according to reports. It also said the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) had not framed a formula for sharing water in distress years in the eight years since it was set up.

Karnataka said this was a rain-deficit year, that several of its areas had been declared drought-hit, and that it had to protect drinking water supplies. It said Tamil Nadu would benefit from north-east monsoon rains in November, which do not help Karnataka, and that the CWMA had considered the issue at its meeting on 8 October, when it directed 3,000 cusecs to flow at Biligundlu for 15 days, according to reports.

Under the Supreme Court's 2018 judgment on the dispute, Karnataka must release 177.25 TMC a year at Biligundlu in a normal year, with the amount cut proportionately in a distress year. Tamil Nadu first went to the court on 3 August, and the court reserved its decision on 12 October, according to reports.

The ruling is a setback for Chief Minister Vijay's TVK government. The opposition AIADMK criticised the state government over the outcome, saying it had filed repeated petitions without result, according to reports.

## Bike taxis

A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh dismissed the Karnataka government's appeal against a Karnataka High Court judgment of 23 January, according to reports. That judgment, by a division bench of then Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice C M Joshi, set aside an order that had required bike-taxi operators to suspend services until the state framed a policy. It held that motorcycles can be registered as transport vehicles and run as contract carriages, "subject to regulatory requirements imposed by the State".

The state had raised concerns about passenger safety and insurance. Auto-rickshaw and taxi associations, which also challenged the judgment, argued that bike taxis without the same obligations would hurt their members. The appeals had been brought against operators including Ola, Uber and Rapido, motorcycle owners and a bike-taxi welfare association.

## What it means

The Cauvery order leaves the sharing of water this season to the CWMA and its regulation committee, which meet regularly to set releases. In Karnataka, bike taxis can continue to operate, but the state can still impose rules on safety, insurance and permits.
